vocabulary.translation: To think / To give an opinion
vocabulary.exampleTranslation: What do you think about the current situation?

vocabulary.exampleTranslation: I think this is a good idea.

grammar.title: Subjunctive vs. Indicative with Opinion Expressions
grammar.explanation:
Whether to use subjunctive or indicative depends on the type of opinion expression:

Indicative (certainty, affirmation):
• Creo que + indicative: Creo que es verdad. (I think it's true.)
• Estoy seguro de que + indicative: Estoy seguro de que tiene razón. (I'm sure he's right.)

Subjunctive (doubt, denial, negation):
• No creo que + subjunctive: No creo que sea verdad. (I don't think it's true.)
• Dudo que + subjunctive: Dudo que tenga razón. (I doubt he's right.)
• Es posible que + subjunctive: Es posible que llueva mañana. (It's possible it will rain tomorrow.)

Key rule: Negating a belief/certainty expression triggers the subjunctive.
